expectations.text: Rejects both the wristbands and the programme listing, removing them from the option set rather than ranking them low.
expectations.evidence: "Drop both ideas."

expectations.text: States that no rewording of the programme line and no redesign of the credential fixes what the discretion request forbids.
expectations.evidence: Only the programme line gets "No rewording fixes that." It makes no equivalent statement that no redesign of the credential would fix it.

expectations.text: Ties that deletion specifically to the guest whose office asked that she not be listed or photographed.
expectations.evidence: "The programme director's office asked that she not be listed or photographed."

expectations.text: Selects a named door list, held by one person, as the access mechanic instead.
expectations.evidence: "Use one named person with one printed door page."

expectations.text: States that publicly only a closed door and somebody standing at it should be legible.
expectations.evidence: It says "Nobody is told the room exists" and "Keep the reception out of the programme entirely", but never states the closed-door-and-person principle.

expectations.text: Requires the invitation to go out individually and privately from the person holding the list, never on a group thread.
expectations.evidence: "Send it individually and privately from the list holder. Never use a group thread."

expectations.text: Bans the word "VIP" in the invitation, at the door, and on any radio or staff channel.
expectations.evidence: "Never say 'VIP', including on the radio"; the invitation is "without 'VIP'".

expectations.text: Limits the door page to the names, alphabetically, and nothing else.
expectations.evidence: "One person, one printed page, names alphabetical." The list table's circulation note adds "The door page carries names and nothing else."

expectations.text: Instructs the door holder to take the name of anyone not on the page, say the owner will come, and fetch them - never to turn someone away with an explanation and never to adjudicate.
expectations.evidence: "A name not on the page: take the name and fetch the owner. Never adjudicate at the door."

expectations.text: Requires the door page to be handed back to the owner at the end rather than left or binned in a public room.
expectations.evidence: "At the end, the page goes back to the owner, not into a bin."

expectations.text: Sets discretion as a binary check: zero guests who asked not to be identified are identifiable to a general attendee as having been in the room.
expectations.evidence: "No photograph, listing, or credential identifies her to a general attendee. Any one of these fails the check."
